evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

claims.text: The literal stem asks whether "you" were approached by community and/or political party representatives; the addressee is unresolved in the supplied item wording, so no interviewer-side or respondent attribution is asserted. The field records only occurrence, not who approached or what was communicated, and codes are 0 = No and 1 = Yes only.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

claims.text: The literal stem asks whether "you" felt threatened during the interview; the addressee is unresolved in the supplied item wording, so no interviewer-side or respondent attribution is asserted. Codes are 0 = No and 1 = Yes only.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: The literal stem asks whether "you" were physically threatened during the interview; the addressee is unresolved in the supplied item wording, and no nesting, implication, co-occurrence, non-coincidence, or directional relationship is asserted. Codes are 0 = No and 1 = Yes only.
Honesty here is the interviewer's three-point reading of the respondent's attitude in this interview, not a verification that any substantive answer was factually correct.

evidence.quote: should not be bound by laws or court decisions

claims.text: Forced-choice plus strength between presidential exemption from laws and courts and presidential obedience; a stated normative position, not an observation of presidential conduct.

evidence.quote: should never intervene in the country's political process

claims.text: Counterposes military non-intervention against a conditional takeover justification keyed to abuse of power; agreement with takeover is a norm statement, not evidence that intervention happened.

evidence.quote: once elected, [members of Parliament] do their jobs?

claims.text: Single-choice attribution of which actor should ensure elected legislators do their jobs, drawn from the fixed actor list: 0 = The President / Executive, 1 = The Parliament / local government council, 2 = Their Political Party, 3 = The Voters, 4 = No One, with special codes -1 = Missing, 8 = Refused, 9 = Don't know, 93 = Not asked in Burkina Faso after 4th of October, 94 = Not asked in country.
Parallel attribution item for the elected president; because the actor list is shared, the two fields can be compared without assuming one accountability model covers both offices.

evidence.quote: criticized, called names, or harassed by others in the community?

claims.text: Four-point likelihood that a woman candidate would face community criticism, name-calling, or harassment; an anticipation judgment about community sanction, distinct from any recorded harassment event.

evidence.quote: to advance the rights and equality of women

claims.text: Effort-level judgment running from much less to much more with an about-right-amount midpoint; it asks whether government action on women's rights is adequate, not whether equality currently obtains.

evidence.quote: most important for our government and society to address?

claims.text: Single nomination among listed women's-rights issues with an explicit none-of-these option and an other category, so it ranks salience rather than measuring severity or incidence.

evidence.quote: using the police and security forces to enforce public health mandates

claims.text: Five-point agreement that police and security enforcement of health mandates is a justified temporary limit on freedoms during a public-health emergency; a conditional trade-off judgment, with a code marking non-applicability by prior COVID experience.

evidence.quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?

claims.text: Sponsor attribution is a respondent belief over a fixed list spanning the survey organization, state, party, media, international actors, and God; it records perceived provenance, not actual commissioning.

evidence.quote: Willing to participate in follow-up surveys

claims.text: Consent-style follow-up willingness whose special not-applicable state separates respondents without a mobile number from those who declined.

inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.
inquiries.question: Among interviews recording an approach by community or party representatives, how do the felt-threat and physical-threat reports distribute against interviews with no approach, and does the physical-threat report ever occur without a felt-threat report?
inquiries.alternatives: Approach present with threat reports at higher rate versus approach present with threat reports no different from no-approach, and the nested contrast of felt-only versus felt-plus-physical threat; either pattern would reframe threats as partially external-pressure rather than purely interviewer-experience events.
inquiries.ceiling: Restricted to interviewer-recorded Yes/No items in fieldwork; denominator is interviews where these items were asked and answered, not all contacted households; no claim about who approached, no causal effect of approach on threat, and no linkage to respondent answers.

inquiries.route: S04/I03 catalog joint then R14–16 if independently qualified roles and selected inquiry; candidate only
inquiries.question: Do respondents who grant the president latitude from laws and courts also accept military takeover when leaders abuse power, or does the rule-of-law position stand apart from the interventionist norm?
inquiries.alternatives: Concordant configuration (presidential latitude with takeover legitimacy) versus dissociated configuration (obedience to law among those accepting takeover, or latitude among those rejecting takeover); dissociation would show the two items tap separate normative commitments rather than one anti-constraint orientation.
inquiries.ceiling: Both are forced-choice self-reports with strength codes and neither/refused/don't-know states; not observations of presidential or military conduct; no country historical material accompanies the packet; eligible only where both items were asked.

inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.
inquiries.question: Within respondents, do the same actors get named for legislator accountability and presidential accountability, or does the president attract a different responsible actor than MPs?
inquiries.alternatives: Same-actor attribution versus office-contingent attribution where voters or party are named for MPs but Parliament or no-one for the president; office-contingent pairing would indicate distinct accountability models rather than a general civic-responsibility stance.
inquiries.ceiling: Nominal single-choice with shared actor list; denominator limited to settings where both items were asked; no inference about actual accountability practices, and refused/don't-know are not substantive actors.

inquiries.route: S04/I03 catalog joint then R14–16 if independently qualified roles and selected inquiry; candidate only
inquiries.question: Do respondents who expect community harassment of a woman candidate differ in effort demands on women's rights and in which issue they name as most important from those expecting little harassment?
inquiries.alternatives: Harassment-anticipating respondents concentrated on doing-more and a specific issue (e.g., gender-based violence) versus harassment-anticipating respondents showing no distinct effort or priority profile; either outcome separates anticipated social sanction from policy demand.
inquiries.ceiling: Cross-sectional associations only among asked-eligible respondents; no causal ordering between perceived sanction and issue priority; none-of-these and other codes retain their special meaning; no claim about actual harassment.

inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.
inquiries.question: Does follow-up willingness track attributing the interview to the survey organization versus to state, party, or media senders?
inquiries.alternatives: Higher willingness concentrated among those naming the survey organization versus willingness not differentiating sender attribution; differentiation would suggest perceived provenance bears on recontact consent rather than consent being a flat fieldwork artifact.
inquiries.ceiling: Willingness denominator excludes the not-applicable neighbors without a mobile number; no claim about actual recontact, no verification of who really commissioned fieldwork, and other/don't-know sponsor codes retained separately.

inquiries.route: S04/I03 catalog joint then R14–16 if independently qualified roles and selected inquiry; candidate only
inquiries.question: Is acceptance of police enforcement of health mandates distributed differently across interviewer-rated respondent honesty levels?
inquiries.alternatives: Mandate acceptance tracking honesty rating versus mandate acceptance flat across honesty ratings; a link would flag the emergency-powers measure as sensitive to interview rapport, a flat pattern would weaken that alternative reading.
inquiries.ceiling: Honesty is interviewer perception, not answer validity; Q63B carries a not-applicable code for prior COVID non-exposure; no causal reading of interviewer rating on expressed attitudes, and eligible only where both were asked.

holds.missing: No fieldwork debrief, incident log, or training record showing whether approach and threat reports were reviewed or acted upon.
holds.why: Whether these interviewer-side items were used in quality control, rather than merely recorded, cannot be established from the item metadata.

holds.missing: No country-level legal or constitutional record of court-obedience controversies, term limits, or military intervention history accompanies these items.
holds.why: The contemporaneous salience of the rule-of-law and intervention contrasts remains unanchored, so rival contextual readings cannot be adjudicated here.

holds.missing: No record of which public-health mandates, enforcement episodes, or gender-rights debates were live during fieldwork.
holds.why: Whether respondents judged experienced conditions rather than hypothetical framings is not determinable from the question texts alone.

holds.missing: No mobile-ownership or recontact design documentation beyond the not-applicable code and the sponsor list.
holds.why: Follow-up consent cannot be scaled to any recontact population, and sponsor attribution cannot be checked against actual commissioning.
